box-braids: A full head of classic medium box braids: individual three-strand plaits, each about 1 cm wide, growing from neat square sections arranged in a staggered brick-lay grid with crisp, clean parts across the whole scalp. Each braid starts with a small, tidy knot at the root and runs firm and uniform down to mid-back length, ending in sealed, slightly tapered tips. The braids hang loose over the shoulders and down the back, with a few draped in front, showing realistic weight, a smooth braid surface and clearly visible interwoven strands. The braids look real and neatly installed by a professional braider.
trancas-nago-retas: A straight-back cornrow style: about 12 to 14 narrow cornrows braided flat and tight against the scalp, running in parallel straight lines from the front hairline over the crown to the nape. Each cornrow is a smooth, raised underhand braid of even width, separated by crisp, perfectly straight, clean scalp parts, and the hairline is neatly braided in. At the nape the cornrows continue as loose, thin three-strand braids that hang to just below the shoulders, with sealed tips. Tidy, sleek, professional finish; the braiding looks real and neatly done.
knotless-braids: A full head of medium knotless box braids: individual three-strand braids about 1 cm wide, set in clean square sections in a staggered grid with sharp, neat parts. There is no knot at the base: each braid begins flat and seamless with the natural hair at the root, then gradually becomes fuller as it goes down, giving a soft, natural-looking base. The braids are lightweight and flexible, hanging loose to mid-back with sealed, tapered ends and natural movement over the shoulders. The braids look real, smooth and neatly installed.
tranca-boxeadora: Two boxer braids: the hair is parted cleanly down the center from the front hairline to the nape, and each side is woven into a tight Dutch braid, with strands crossed under so the braid stands out raised from the head. Each braid starts at the front hairline near the temple and runs close to the scalp over the side and back of the head, behind the ear. Below the nape, each continues as a regular three-strand plait hanging over the shoulders to about chest level, ending in a neat tip. Smooth, tight, sporty finish with a few soft baby hairs at the hairline. Keep the natural hair texture.
twist-senegalesa: Senegalese twists: a full head of medium rope twists, each about 1 cm thick, made by twisting two smooth strands around each other in a tight, uniform, spiraling rope pattern. They grow from neat square parts arranged in a staggered grid and hang loose to mid-back. The twists are sleek and glossy with a smooth, silky surface, consistent thickness from root to end, and neatly sealed tips that do not unravel. They fall naturally over the shoulders with realistic weight and movement; the twists look real and neatly installed.
fulani-braids: Fulani braids: a single cornrow runs straight back along the center of the head from the front hairline to the crown, flanked on each side by a few cornrows braided flat from the upper sides of the head forward and down toward the temples, ending as loose braids that hang in front of the ears and alongside the jawline. The rest of the hair at the crown and back is in loose, medium box braids. All loose braids hang to mid-back with sealed tips. Crisp, clean parts, sleek flat cornrows and a tidy hairline, without beads; the braiding looks real and neatly installed.
boho-braids: Boho knotless braids: medium knotless box braids, about 1 cm wide, set in neat square parts and hanging loose to mid-back or slightly longer. Soft, defined, loose spiral curls are left out along the length of every braid, so curly pieces spill out between the plaits all over the head, from near the roots down, creating an airy, bohemian cloud of curls. Each braid ends in several centimeters of loose, bouncy curls instead of a sealed tip, and a few curly tendrils fall around the hairline. Romantic, lived-in, voluminous look; the braids and curls look real and neatly installed.
faux-locs: Classic faux locs: a full head of medium locs, about 1.5 cm thick, installed on square parts in a staggered grid. Each loc is tightly wrapped and firm, with a slightly textured, matte, natural-looking loc surface, uniform thickness from root to end and neatly sealed, slightly tapered ends. The locs hang straight and heavy to mid-back, some falling over the shoulders and the rest down the back. Neat roots with clean parts; the locs look like real, mature locs, neatly installed.
dreadlocks: Natural mature dreadlocks: a full head of medium locs, about 1 to 1.5 cm thick, formed from the natural hair and grown out from the roots, falling to the shoulder blades. Each loc is cylindrical and densely matted with a realistic organic texture: a slightly fuzzy surface, small variations in thickness and gently rounded ends, while still neat and well maintained. The roots are tidy with a little natural new growth, the parts are organic and irregular, and the locs hang with natural weight, some falling over the shoulders. Authentic, real-looking locs.
trancas-nago-grossas: Ghana braids in the feed-in style: 6 to 8 bold, thick cornrows braided flat and tight against the scalp, running straight back from the front hairline over the crown to the nape. Each cornrow starts narrow and neat at the hairline and gradually becomes thicker toward the back, giving a smooth, tapered, raised effect, with crisp, straight, clean parts between them. Beyond the nape the braids continue as thick loose plaits hanging to mid-back with sealed tips. Sleek, polished, uniform finish; the braids look real and neatly installed.
box-braids-jumbo: Jumbo box braids: a full head of very thick box braids, each about 2.5 to 3 cm wide, built on large square parts, roughly 20 to 30 braids in total, in a staggered grid with crisp, clean parts. Each chunky three-strand braid starts at a neat base and stays bold and uniform down to mid-back, ending in sealed tips. The heavy braids fall loose over the shoulders and down the back with clearly visible plait texture and realistic weight. The braids look real and neatly installed.
tranca-embutida: A single classic French braid: all the hair is gathered smoothly back from the front hairline with no part and woven into one centered French braid that starts at the top of the head and runs close to the scalp down the back of the head, picking up hair from both sides as it goes so the woven sections lie flat. Below the nape it continues as a regular three-strand plait hanging down the back to about the shoulder blades, ending in a neat tapered tip. Smooth, tidy finish with gently loosened braid loops and a few soft wisps at the hairline. Keep the natural hair texture.
crochet-braids-cacheado: Curly crochet braids: a full, voluminous head of defined, bouncy spiral curls, each curl about 2 cm in diameter, installed with the crochet method over hidden flat cornrows so no braids or parts are visible and the result looks like loose natural curly hair. The curls reach from the collarbones to just below the shoulders, forming a big rounded shape with lots of volume at the crown and sides and soft curly pieces around the hairline. Each curl is well defined, springy and separated, with natural variation and a little frizz. Seamless, real-looking install.
microtrancas: Micro box braids: hundreds of very fine braids, each only about 3 to 4 mm thick, from tiny, precise square parts covering the whole head. The braids are dense and uniform, so the overall look is fluid and swingy, almost like loose straight hair, with the fine plait pattern visible up close. They hang to mid-back with neat sealed tips, fall freely over the shoulders and move together as one soft mass. Even tension and clean tiny parts at the roots; the braids look real and meticulously installed.
box-braids-bob: Bob box braids: a full head of small-to-medium box braids, about 6 to 8 mm wide, set in neat square parts in a staggered grid and finished at a blunt bob length that ends between the chin and the jawline all around. The braids have neat sealed tips and swing freely around the jaw in a rounded bob silhouette with a slight outward bend, leaving the neck visible. Clean parts and tidy roots; the braids look real and neatly installed.
nago-desenhada: Designer cornrows: about 10 to 14 thin-to-medium cornrows braided flat and tight against the scalp in a bold geometric pattern, with sharp zigzag lines running back from the front hairline and a few cornrows angling around to form a symmetrical design on the top and sides of the head. The scalp parts are crisp, clean and precise, outlining the design clearly. At the nape the cornrows continue as loose thin braids hanging past the shoulders with sealed tips. Sleek, neat, artistic finish; the braiding looks real and expertly done.
lemonade-braids: Lemonade braids: about 14 to 20 thin-to-medium cornrows braided flat against the scalp, all sweeping diagonally from a deep side part across the top of the head toward the opposite side and curving gently around behind the ear. The cornrows are sleek and even, with crisp, clean, parallel parts. They continue as long, slim loose braids that gather and cascade over one shoulder down to the waist, with sealed tips. Elegant, glossy, neat finish; the braiding looks real and neatly installed.
butterfly-locs: Butterfly locs: a full head of medium faux locs, about 1.5 cm thick, with a deliberately distressed, bohemian texture: small loose loops and bubbles of soft hair pop out along each loc, creating a fluffy, airy, uneven surface instead of a smooth wrap. The locs hang to just past the shoulders, around armpit length, with slightly curly, open ends. Neat parts at the roots, lightweight movement and a soft, messy-chic finish; the locs look real and neatly installed.
twist-out-definido: A twist out: natural coily hair worn loose after two-strand twists have been unraveled, giving a full head of defined, elongated, chunky coils with a rope-like twisted wave pattern, each section clearly separated and glossy. The hair forms a big, rounded, voluminous shape at about chin-to-shoulder length, with lift at the roots, fluffed volume at the crown and sides, softly defined ends, a little natural frizz and a neat hairline. Moisturized, healthy, real-looking finish.
two-strand-twists: Natural two-strand twists made on the natural hair, without extensions: the whole head is sectioned into small square parts and each section is twisted into a neat, defined two-strand twist about 6 to 8 mm thick, with a soft, slightly fuzzy coily texture and a clearly visible rope pattern. The twists are dense and full, standing out with natural volume and falling to around chin-to-shoulder length, with naturally coiled ends. Moisturized, defined finish with healthy natural shine; looks real and neatly done.
box-braids-longas: Extra-long box braids: a full head of small-to-medium box braids, about 7 to 8 mm wide, on neat square parts in a staggered grid with crisp parts and small, tidy bases. The braids are uniform and very long, falling past the waist toward the hips, with neatly sealed tips. They hang loose, with some draped over the shoulders and down the front and the rest falling straight down the back with realistic heavy weight and swing. The braids look real and neatly installed.
coque-box-braids: Box braids in a high bun: a full head of medium box braids, about 1 cm wide, on neat square parts, all smoothly gathered upward from the nape, sides and hairline and wound into a large, rounded top-knot bun at the high crown. The braids lie neat and smooth toward the crown with a visible braid pattern and clean parts, and the bun shows the braids coiled around each other with the ends tucked in. Two thin braids are left loose by the temples, hanging to the jawline. Elegant, neat, real-looking install.
rabo-de-cavalo-nago: A cornrow braided ponytail: about 12 to 16 slim cornrows braided flat and tight against the scalp, all running upward and inward from the front hairline, sides and nape toward a single point at the high crown, with crisp, clean, converging parts. At the crown the braids gather into a high ponytail, its base wrapped with one of the braids, and long, slim loose braids cascade from the top of the head down the back to mid-back, with sealed tips. Sleek, sculpted, glamorous finish; the braiding looks real and neatly installed.
tribal-braids: Tribal braids: the front half of the head is braided in sleek cornrows running in mixed directions, a few straight back from the hairline, some angled toward the temples and sides, and one curved cornrow outlining the side of the hairline, creating a bold, asymmetric pattern with crisp, clean parts. The back half of the head is in loose medium box braids on square parts. The front cornrows flow into loose braids that blend with the rest, all hanging to mid-back with sealed tips. Neat, defined finish without beads; the braiding looks real and neatly installed.
passion-twists: Passion twists: a full head of medium two-strand twists, about 1.2 cm thick, made with soft, springy, wavy-textured hair, so each twist has a loose, fluffy, slightly bumpy rope pattern rather than a sleek finish. The twists hang to the shoulder blades, with a few centimeters of open, curly, wavy ends at the tips. Soft, airy volume, some fine curly wisps, neat square parts at the roots and natural bounce; the twists look real and neatly installed.
french-curl-braids: French curl braids: medium knotless braids, about 1 cm wide, set in neat square parts and braided only from the roots down to around shoulder level; from there each braid opens into long, loose, silky, bouncy spiral curls that continue down to mid-back. The result is a sleek braided upper section and a full, flowing curtain of soft, shiny, loosely spiraled curly ends below the shoulders. Neat roots, smooth braids and defined, swingy curls with natural movement; real-looking and neatly installed.
bantu-knots: Bantu knots: the hair is divided into about 10 to 14 neat sections with crisp, clean parts forming triangles and squares across the scalp, and each section is twisted tightly and wound around itself into a small, firm, coiled knot sitting flat on the scalp, about 3 to 4 cm in diameter. The knots are evenly distributed over the top, crown, sides and back, with all lengths tucked into the knots and no loose hair hanging down. Smooth, glossy, sculptural, neat finish; looks real and expertly done.
flat-twist: Flat twists: about 8 to 12 two-strand twists made flat and close to the scalp, running straight back from the front hairline toward the nape, like cornrows but with a twisted rope pattern instead of a braid. Each flat twist is smooth, defined and even, with clean straight parts between the rows. At the back, the twists finish as loose two-strand twists hanging to about the shoulders, with soft, coiled ends. Neat, natural, moisturized finish; looks real and neatly done.
goddess-locs: Goddess locs: a full head of medium faux locs, about 1.5 cm thick, on neat square parts, each smoothly wrapped from root to end, with soft, loose spiral curls left out along the length, so curly strands peek out between the locs. Each loc ends in several centimeters of open, bouncy, defined curls. The locs hang to mid-back with flowing movement over the shoulders. Bohemian, airy finish with a few curly tendrils around the hairline; the locs look real and neatly installed.
braid-out-ondulado: A braid out: natural textured hair worn loose after three-strand braids have been unraveled, giving a full head of uniform, defined, crimped zigzag waves with soft S-shaped bends from roots to ends, separated into distinct glossy sections. The hair has a big, fluffy, rounded volume at chin-to-shoulder length, with lift at the crown and sides, slightly tousled ends and a soft natural frizz. Moisturized, healthy, real-looking finish.
box-braids-meio-preso: Half-up box braids: a full head of medium box braids, about 1 cm wide, on neat square parts. The braids of the top section, from the front hairline back to the crown and above the temples, are gathered up and wound into a neat, rounded top-knot bun at the high crown, with the ends tucked in. The braids from the sides and back hang loose to mid-back with sealed tips, falling over the shoulders, and two thin braids hang loose by the temples. Clean parts and a real-looking, neat install.
tranca-espinha-de-peixe: A loose side fishtail braid: all the hair is brushed softly back and to one side with no harsh part and gathered low behind the ear on that side into a single fishtail braid that falls over the front of one shoulder to about chest level. The braid is woven from many thin crisscrossing sections, creating a fine herringbone pattern, gently pulled apart for a fuller, softly undone look, and it ends in a neat tapered tip. A few soft wisps are left loose around the hairline. Keep the natural hair texture.
tranca-coroa: A crown braid: all the hair is woven into one braid that wraps around the head like a halo, starting behind one ear, running across the top of the head just behind the front hairline, continuing down the other side and around the back above the nape, and ending tucked invisibly into its own beginning. The braid sits flat and secure, slightly pulled apart for a soft, full, romantic look, with no hair hanging down. A few soft wisps fall at the hairline and temples. Keep the natural hair texture.
stitch-braids: Stitch braids: 6 to 10 medium cornrows braided straight back from the front hairline to the nape, flat and tight against the scalp, each made with the stitch technique so it shows evenly spaced horizontal stitch lines, small clean ladder-like segments, along both sides of every braid. The parts are razor-straight and crisp. Past the nape the braids continue as loose, uniform plaits hanging to mid-back with sealed tips. Sleek, sharply defined, precise finish; the braids look real and neatly installed.
nago-curvas: Curved cornrows: about 10 to 14 thin-to-medium cornrows braided flat and tight against the scalp in smooth, flowing S-curves that sweep back from the front hairline, swirl gently around the crown and curve around the sides behind the ears, all running parallel to each other. The parts between them are crisp and clean, following the same wavy lines. At the nape the cornrows continue as loose thin braids hanging past the shoulders with sealed tips. Sleek, fluid, artistic pattern; the braiding looks real and expertly done.
soft-locs: Soft locs: a full head of medium faux locs, about 1.5 cm thick, loosely wrapped with soft, fluffy, wavy hair, giving each loc a plush, slightly fuzzy, lightweight texture with gentle bumps rather than a tight, sleek wrap. The locs are flexible, swing freely and hang to mid-back, with soft, slightly open ends. Neat parts at the roots and an airy, effortless finish; the locs look real and neatly installed.
marley-twists: Marley twists: a full head of medium-to-thick two-strand twists, about 1.5 cm wide, made with coarse, kinky, afro-textured hair, so the twists have a matte, slightly fuzzy surface like natural coily hair rather than a sleek finish. They grow from neat square parts and hang to the shoulder blades, with full, chunky bodies and neatly sealed ends. Natural volume and movement; the twists look real and neatly installed.
spring-twists: Spring twists: a full head of short, springy, coiled twists, about 8 to 10 mm thick, with a tight, bouncy, spring-like coil texture and a slightly fluffy surface. They are installed on small neat parts and hang to around chin-to-shoulder length, bouncing outward with lots of airy volume to create a full, rounded, playful shape. The ends are soft and naturally coiled; the twists look real and neatly installed.
island-twists: Island twists: a full head of medium knotless two-strand twists, about 1 cm thick, starting seamlessly at the root with no knot and made with silky, slightly wavy hair, so the twists look soft and lightweight. Loose, defined curly strands are left out along the length, peeking out between the twists for a carefree, beachy, boho look, and each twist ends in several centimeters of open curls. The twists hang to mid-back with flowing movement; real-looking and neatly installed.
sisterlocks: Sisterlocks: hundreds of very fine, uniform microlocs, each about 2 to 3 mm thick, formed from the natural hair on a precise, tiny grid of parts across the whole scalp. The locs are smooth, tight and consistent, light and flexible, falling with fluid movement past the shoulders to around the shoulder blades, almost like loose hair, with neat rounded ends. Tidy roots and a defined hairline; authentic, mature, real-looking locs.
dreads-iniciais: Starter locs: a full head of short, newly started locs made with the comb-coil method, each a neat, tight cylindrical coil about 8 mm thick, set on a clean, evenly spaced grid of square parts. The coils are short, about 5 to 8 cm long, standing slightly up and out from the head in a rounded, full shape around the crown and sides and ending at about ear to jaw level, with soft, closed, rounded tips. Defined, glossy, moisturized coils; authentic, real-looking starter locs.
twist-jumbo: Jumbo Havana twists: a full head of very thick two-strand twists, about 2.5 to 3 cm wide, on large square parts, roughly 25 to 35 twists in total, made with fluffy, airy, lightly textured hair, so each twist is chunky, full and soft with a matte, natural surface. They hang to mid-back with sealed ends, creating a bold, voluminous shape over the shoulders and down the back. Neat roots; the twists look real and neatly installed.
box-braids-triangulares: Triangle-part box braids: a full head of medium box braids, about 1 cm wide, where every braid grows from a triangular section instead of a square one, so the scalp shows a crisp, clean, tessellated pattern of triangles across the top, sides and back of the head. Each braid starts with a neat base and runs uniform down to mid-back with sealed tips, hanging loose over the shoulders and back. Sharp, precise parting; the braids look real and neatly installed.
